notes: Dev-split RBox revision (10 queries). Flips a property that holds: by the second law (Clausius), heat flows spontaneously only from a hotter body to a colder one, and temperature orders bodies, so if a spontaneously transfers heat to b, b does not spontaneously transfer heat to a; transfers_heat_to is asymmetric in RELATIONS.md, and the edit makes it symmetric. Changed in review: the record first used the catalogue's wording "spontaneously transfers net heat to". Net heat cannot flow both ways between the same two bodies by the meaning of "net", so the edited world contradicted its own words and a model answering no might be reading "net" correctly. The prompts now say "spontaneously transfers heat to": the asymmetry then comes from physics (the second law and the ordering of temperatures), which the counterfactual overrides, not from the definition of the predicate. The catalogue row (RELATIONS.md, not edited here) still reads "net heat"; the relation is the same. Residual risk, recorded: a model may still treat "heat" as net energy flow by definition (as thermodynamics textbooks do), which pulls it back to the original answers; that is the stored property resisting the edit rather than an incoherent prompt. The direct question asks the edited property itself ("symmetric?", no then yes). The instance questions give one transfer in the prompt and ask what follows; the objects are named but carry no temperatures, so stored physics (a hot coffee cools) cannot answer them without the relation property. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: direct no, first instance (does it rule out the converse) yes, asked again in Chinese and Spanish, second instance (does the converse follow) no; originals are 3 yes and 2 no. Near unrelated asks the same property (symmetry) of another physical relation (is heavier than), whose answer (no) differs from the direct question's new answer. records/physics has no RBox record on transfers_heat_to.
